s.d: a person who does not belong to the group of believers in Christ{N:001}
s.g: non-Christian
s.c: In ⟦1 Corinthians 7:15|1 Corinthians 7:15⟧ it may be necessary to indicate the so-called goal of belief or trust, for example, ‘if one who is not a believer in Christ’ or ‘if the one who is not a follower of Christ.’

s.dp: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior › Honesty, Sincerity
s.d: the quality of sincerity as an expression of singleness of purpose or motivation
s.g: sincerity; purity of motive

s.d: an act of generosity
s.g: generosity; liberality; to act in a generous manner

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Health, Vigor, Strength
s.d: pertaining to being healthy, with the implication of sound, proper functioning (in the NT with particular reference to the eyes)
s.g: to be healthy; to be sound
s.c: For another interpretation of ἁπλοῦς in ⟦Luke 11:34|Luke 11:34⟧, see LN 57.107. See also LN 23.149.

s.d: pertaining to willing and generous giving
s.g: generous; generously; liberal
s.c: In ⟦Matthew 6:22|Matthew 6:22⟧ and the corresponding passage in ⟦Luke 11:34|Luke 11:34⟧, most scholars understand ἁπλοῦς in the sense of ‘to be healthy’ or ‘to be sound’ (see LN 23.132).

s.d: pertaining to willing and generous giving
s.g: generous; generously; liberal

s.d: a marker of dissociation, implying a rupture from a former association
s.g: from; separated from

s.dp: Case › Source of Event or Activity
s.d: a marker of source of an implied event
s.g: from; by
s.c: In ⟦Matthew 5:42|Matthew 5:42⟧ ἀπό also marks the one who would be the agent of loaning.

s.dp: Spacial Extensions › Extension From a Source
s.d: extension from or away from a source
s.g: from; away from

s.d: a marker of a part of a whole, whether consisting of countables or of mass
s.g: one of; one among; a part of

s.d: a marker of the substance of which something consists or out of which it is made
s.g: of; consisting of; out of; made of

s.dp: Case › Agent, Personal or Nonpersonal, Causative or Immediate, Direct or Indirect
s.d: a marker of agent which may also be regarded as a source{N:003}
s.g: by; from
s.c: The expression ζητοῦντες … δόξαν in ⟦1 Thessalonians 2:6|1 Thessalonians 2:6⟧ clearly indicates an event of ‘seeking to be honored’ or ‘seeking to be given glory.’ In such an instance, ἀπό serves to mark not only the agent but also a source.

s.d: a marker of instrument which serves as a source of information or reason
s.g: by; from

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Point of Time: Until, Delay, Still, From
s.d: a marker of the extent of time from a point in the past
s.g: since; from

s.d: a marker of cause or reason, with focus upon the source{N:005}
s.g: because of

s.d: a marker of one who is responsible for an event or state
s.g: by; on (the basis of); of; upon

s.d: (an idiom, literally: from a part) the state of being part of something
s.g: being part of; as a part of; in part; partially

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
s.d: (an idiom, literally: from a part) pertaining to a relatively short period of time, with emphasis upon the temporary nature of the event or state
s.g: not long; temporary; for a little while; for a while

s.d: (an idiom, literally: from one) a sequence of single units, one after another
s.g: one after another; one by one

s.dp: Time › Duration of Time with Reference to Some Point of Time: Until, Delay, Still, From
s.d: an exceedingly long period of time from an assumed beginning up to the present
s.g: since all time; from all ages past; from the beginning of time

s.dp: Be, Become, Exist, Happen › Change of State
s.d: a marker of a change of state
s.g: from … to; to; for

s.dp: Time › A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
s.d: (an idiom, literally: from ancient days) a point of time preceding another point of time, with a considerable interval
s.g: long ago; some time ago
s.c: This reference to Peter having been chosen by God sometime before to bring the gospel to the Gentiles can hardly be regarded as a reference to ancient times, though some persons understand this to mean that God’s decision was made at the beginning of time. The usage of ἀφ᾽ ἡμερῶν ἀρχαίων is probably designed to emphasize the established nature of God’s decision for Peter to take the gospel to the Gentiles beginning with the centurion Cornelius. The fact that this was relatively early in the development of the church may also serve to explain the use of the idiom.

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to get off or to depart, as from a ship
s.g: to disembark; to get off

s.d: (an idiom, literally: to go away into) to result in a state
s.g: to result in; to lead to

s.d: to remove a piece of clothing quickly and cast it aside
s.g: to throw off; to remove and throw aside

s.d: to cause a state to cease by force and with the implication of elimination
s.g: to remove; to drive out; to do away with

s.d: to keep thinking about, without having one’s attention distracted
s.g: to think about; to fix one’s attention on

s.d: (derivative of ἀποβάλλω ‘to reject,’ not occurring in the NT) that which is to be rejected
s.g: something to be rejected
s.c: The closest equivalent of ἀπόβλητος in a number of languages is ‘something to be thrown away’ or ‘something to refuse.’

s.dp: Association › Belong To, Be Included in the Membership of, Be Excluded From
s.d: the removal of someone from a particular association
s.g: rejection; elimination
s.c: In rendering this clause in ⟦Romans 11:15|Romans 11:15⟧, it may be necessary to indicate more specifically the participants and the implied relationships, for example, ‘for if their being rejected meant that people in general were reconciled to God.’

s.d: the event of ceasing to exist
s.g: loss; destruction

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἀπογίνομαι ‘to die,’ not occurring in the NT) to cease, with a complete and abrupt change
s.g: to cease; to stop
s.c: It is possible that in the translation of this phrase in ⟦1 Peter 2:24|1 Peter 2:24⟧ one might wish to preserve the figurative form and translate as ‘dying to sin.’ For another interpretation of ἀπογίνομαι in ⟦1 Peter 2:24|1 Peter 2:24⟧, see LN 74.27.

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of ἀπογίνομαι ‘to die,’ not occurring in the NT) to be unable to respond or react to any impulse or desire
s.g: to be dead to; to not respond to; to have no part in
s.c: In a number of languages it is extremely difficult to speak of ‘dying to sin.’ In some instances one can preserve the figurative meaning by an expression such as ‘to be like dead as far as desiring to sin’ or ‘to be like a corpse as far as temptations to sin are concerned.’|For another interpretation of ἀπογίνομαι in ⟦1 Peter 2:24|1 Peter 2:24⟧, see LN 68.40.

s.d: the event of registering persons in connection with taking a census
s.g: census
s.c: One may construct a descriptive equivalent of ‘census’ by speaking of ‘when everyone’s name is taken down and he is counted’ or ‘a time when the government writes down everyone’s name on a list’ or ‘… in books.’

s.d: to register someone, often in connection with taking a census
s.g: to register; to put on a census list
s.c: In a number of languages the equivalent of ἀπογράφω is simply ‘to have one’s name put in a book’ or ‘to have one’s name put in a list of those living in a particular place.’|In ⟦Hebrews 12:23|Hebrews 12:23⟧ (καὶ ἐκκλησίᾳ πρωτοτόκων ἀπογεγραμμένων ἐν οὐρανοῖς ‘and at the gathering of the firstborn, whose names are written in heaven’) ἀπογράφω is used in a figurative sense, but it is usually translated more or less literally.

s.dp: Know › Well Known, Clearly Shown, Revealed
s.d: to cause something to be known as genuine, with possible focus upon the source of such knowledge
s.g: to demonstrate; to show; to make clearly known

s.d: to cause something to be known publicly
s.g: to show publicly; to demonstrate publicly

s.d: to demonstrate that something is true
s.g: to show to be true; to prove

s.dp: Know › Well Known, Clearly Shown, Revealed
s.d: (derivative of {L:ἀποδείκνυμι<SDBG:ἀποδείκνυμι:000000>}[a] to demonstrate, to show, {D:28.50}) the means by which one knows that something is a fact.{N:001}{N:002}
s.g: proof; evidence; verification; indication

s.d: to give a tenth of one’s income
s.g: to give a tenth; to tithe

s.d: to cause someone to pay a tenth
s.g: to collect tithes; to exact tithes from
s.c: In a number of languages there are problems involved in speaking of ‘a tenth,’ and accordingly there are difficulties in formulating expressions about ‘tithing.’ In some languages one may speak of ‘a tenth’ as ‘one part of ten parts’ or ‘one part together with nine parts.’ ‘To tithe’ may be rendered as ‘from ten parts to pay one part’ or ‘to pay one part and to keep nine parts.’

s.dp: Attitudes and Emotions › Acceptable To, To Be Pleased With
s.d: pertaining to that which is pleasing in view of its being acceptable
s.g: pleasing; acceptable
s.c: In a number of languages it is necessary to restructure expressions containing ‘acceptable to’ or ‘pleasing to.’ For example, in ⟦Acts 10:35|Acts 10:35⟧ it may be necessary to translate ‘God accepts whoever worships him and does what is right’ or ‘God is pleased with whoever worships him and does what is right.’ Similarly, in ⟦1 Timothy 2:3|1 Timothy 2:3⟧ one may translate ‘this is good, and God our Savior likes it’ or ‘… is happy because of it.’

s.d: to accept the presence of a person with friendliness{N:001}
s.g: to welcome; to receive; to accept; to have as a guest

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Accept As True
s.d: to come to believe something to be true and to respond accordingly, with some emphasis upon the source
s.g: to accept; to receive; acceptance; reception

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Acknowledge
s.d: to recognize or acknowledge the truth of something, normally implying something good
s.g: to acknowledge; to recognize; to think about favorably
s.c: See discussion of ⟦Acts 24:3|Acts 24:3⟧ at LN 83.8.

s.dp: Linear Movement › Leave, Depart, Flee, Escape, Send
s.d: to journey away from one’s home or home country, implying for a considerable period of time and at quite a distance
s.g: to leave home on a journey; to be away from home on a journey

s.dp: Existence in Space › Be in a Place
s.d: pertaining to being away from where one usually resides{N:001}
s.g: to be away from home; to be away on a journey

s.d: to return to someone what belongs to that person
s.g: to return; to give back

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Pay, Price, Cost
s.d: to make a payment, with the implication of such a payment being in response to an incurred obligation{N:001}
s.g: to pay; to render

s.d: to recompense someone, whether positively or negatively, depending upon what the individual deserves
s.g: to reward; to recompense

s.d: to cause to happen what has been promised, often in relation to vows or oaths
s.g: to cause to happen; to do; to pay back

s.dp: Case › Agent of a Numerable Event
s.d: a marker of an agent relation with a numerable event, with the probable implication of some transfer involved
s.g: to make; to perform; to do; to give

s.dp: Possess, Transfer, Exchange › Sell, Buy, Price
s.d: to dispose of property or provide services in exchange for money or other valuable considerations
s.g: to sell
s.c: πιπράσκω and ἀποδίδομαι (ἀποδίδωμι) may also be used to refer to selling a person into slavery. Note, for example, πιπράσκω in ⟦Matthew 18:25|Matthew 18:25⟧ (ἐκέλευσεν αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος πραθῆναι ‘his master ordered him to be sold as a slave’) and ἀποδίδομαι in ⟦Acts 7:9|Acts 7:9⟧ (οἱ πατριάρχαι ζηλώσαντες τὸν Ἰωσὴφ ἀπέδοντο εἰς Αἴγυπτον ‘the patriarchs were jealous of Joseph and sold him to be a slave in Egypt’).|In a number of languages, however, it may be important to use a distinctive term for selling a person into slavery. In fact, it may be necessary to describe the event rather explicitly, for example, ‘to receive money for handing a person over to someone else to be a slave.’|In ⟦Romans 7:14|Romans 7:14⟧ πιπράσκω is used figuratively in the phrase πεπραμένος ὑπὸ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν ‘sold as a slave to sin,’ in the sense that sin is personified as the master.

s.d: to cause or instigate divisions between people
s.g: to cause divisions
s.c: ‘To cause divisions’ may be expressed in a number of languages in idiomatic ways, for example, ‘to cause people to turn their backs on one another’ or ‘to cause people to no longer speak to one another’ or ‘to cause people to form parties against one another.’ For another interpretation of ἀποδιορίζω in ⟦Jude 1:19|Jude 1:19⟧, see LN 30.116.

s.dp: Think › To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
s.d: to judge that there is a significant distinction between two or more objects or events
s.g: to make a distinction between; to draw a line between; to separate one from another
s.c: In ⟦Jude 1:19|Jude 1:19⟧ the specific distinction between ‘spiritual and unspiritual persons’ comes from the context, as suggested in the New English Bible. For another interpretation of ἀποδιορίζω in ⟦Jude 1:19|Jude 1:19⟧, see LN 39.16.

s.dp: Think › To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
s.d: to judge someone or something as not being worthy or genuine and thus something to be rejected
s.g: to regard as not worthy; to reject

s.dp: Hold a View, Believe, Trust › Accept As True
s.d: to come to believe something to be true and to respond accordingly, with some emphasis upon the source
s.g: to accept; to receive; acceptance; reception

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: (an idiom, literally: putting off of the dwelling, {D:7.8}) euphemistic expression for dying
s.g: to die

s.d: small structure for storing agricultural produce; normally made of stone
s.g: barn; storehouse
s.c: In a number of languages an important distinction is made between buildings used to store farm produce and those which may be warehouses for other types of material.

s.d: to keep safe that which is of great value
s.g: to treasure up; to keep safe
s.c: There are certain problems involved in the combination of ἀποθησαυρίζοντας and θεμέλιον, for this would constitute a type of mixed metaphor. In some languages, therefore, it may be useful to speak of θεμέλιον in ⟦1 Timothy 6:19|1 Timothy 6:19⟧ as ‘a help’ or even as ‘something valuable.’

s.d: to crowd in hard against{N:001}
s.g: to press against; to crowd against

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: the process of dying
s.g: to die; death
s.c: In a number of languages clear distinctions are made in the use of terms for dying on the basis of the manner or circumstances of death. For example, one term may refer to death primarily as the result of old age, while another term may refer to death caused by sickness, and still other terms may be used for death caused by violence. Careful distinctions must be used in determining the choice of terms based on particular contexts.|In ⟦John 6:50|John 6:50⟧ ἀποθνῄσκω must be understood in a spiritual rather than in a strictly literal sense. This bold figurative language is characteristic of the Gospel of John and should not be eliminated, though in some languages a strictly literal translation may be understood only in a literal sense and thus lead to misinterpretation. In some instances, therefore, it may be necessary to suggest the metaphorical significance by translating ‘he will not, as it were, die.’

s.dp: Physiological Processes and States › Live, Die
s.d: to be in imminent danger of dying
s.g: to face death; to be likely to die
s.c: It would also be possible to render καθ᾽ ἡμέραν ἀποθνῄσκω in ⟦1 Corinthians 15:31|1 Corinthians 15:31⟧ as ‘I am in danger of being killed each day.’

s.d: (a figurative extension of meaning of {L:ἀποθνῄσκω<SDBG:ἀποθνῄσκω:000000>}[a] ‘to die,’ {D:23.99}) to be unable to respond or react to any impulse or desire
s.g: to be dead to; to not respond to; to have no part in
s.c: In a number of languages it is extremely difficult to speak of ‘dying to sin.’ In some instances one can preserve the figurative meaning by an expression such as ‘to be like dead as far as desiring to sin’ or ‘to be like a corpse as far as temptations to sin are concerned.’
